# Striatum Agent Guide

This guide is the generic-profile equivalent of the Claude Code
skill bundle. Concatenate it into your agent's system prompt or
`cat` it before driving a Striatum workflow.

Striatum is a local-first runner whose authoritative live state lives in a
daemon-owned PostgreSQL instance under a `repository_id` scope per target
repository (D094 / RFC 0043). `.striatum/` next to the target repo is
operational scratch only. The runner — not your prose, terminal output, or
direct database access — advances state through daemon MCP/RPC methods.

## Scaffold

Bring a target repo from "no `.striatum/`" to "a run that's ready
to claim work":

- `striatum repo add` — Register the target repo with the daemon (live state lives in the daemon's PostgreSQL under a `repository_id` scope per D094 / RFC 0043).
- `striatum workflow generate` — Render a starter `workflow.json` plus role/prompt stubs from a catalog shape.
- `striatum workflow validate` — Validate a workflow file; non-zero exit on error.
- `striatum run prepare` — Snapshot the workflow and prepare a run id.
- `striatum run start` — Transition a prepared run to `running` and enqueue eligible root jobs for registered sessions to claim.
- `striatum branch confirm` — Confirm or create the run's working branch.

Common pattern:

```bash
striatum --repo /path/to/target init
striatum --repo /path/to/target workflow validate path/to/workflow.json
tools/call run.prepare {"workflow":"path/to/workflow.json"}
tools/call run.start {"run_id":"<id>"}
```

After a repo is registered for the first time, ask the operator whether they
want to install any optional, third-party agent skills. These are **not part of
Striatum** — they install agent-side and Striatum does not fetch, vendor, or
maintain them. Install only the ones the operator explicitly confirms;
otherwise continue without them. Currently suggested: **adhd** — divergent
ideation (parallel idea branches under different cognitive frames, then
critic-prune and deepen survivors); Claude-only; install only if confirmed:
`npx skills add UditAkhourii/adhd`

## Claim loop

The core MCP method sequence for actually doing work:

- `striatum register-session` — Open an agent session for a (role, lane) pair.
- `striatum claim-next` — Claim the next ready work packet for a session.
- `striatum ack` — Acknowledge a claimed packet and start work.
- `striatum heartbeat` — Extend the active lease while work continues.
- `striatum publish-artifact` — Publish a build artifact for a job.
- `striatum verdict` — Record a non-finding verdict for a review job.
- `striatum submit-review` — Publish a finding artifact + verdict in one call.
- `striatum complete` — Mark a non-review job complete.
- `striatum worktree create` — Create the per-job git worktree (RFC 0008).
- `striatum worktree release` — Release a per-job worktree when work is done.

Common pattern:

```json
{"method":"tools/list","params":{"repository_id":"<repository-id>"}}
{"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"session.register","repository_id":"<repository-id>","arguments":{"run_id":"<run-id>","role":"<role>","lane":"<lane>"}}}
{"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"work.await_packet","repository_id":"<repository-id>","arguments":{"session_id":"<session-id>","lease_seconds":1800}}}
{"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"work.ack","repository_id":"<repository-id>","arguments":{"session_id":"<session-id>","message_id":"<message-id>","lease_id":"<lease-id>"}}}
{"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"artifact.publish","repository_id":"<repository-id>","arguments":{"session_id":"<session-id>","job_id":"<job-id>","lease_id":"<lease-id>","kind":"<kind>","logical_name":"<logical-name>","path":"<repo-relative-path>"}}}
{"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"work.complete","repository_id":"<repository-id>","arguments":{"session_id":"<session-id>","job_id":"<job-id>","lease_id":"<lease-id>","summary":"completed"}}}
```

For review jobs, replace the last two steps with
`review.submit` and `verdict` set to
`{accept,accept_with_findings,needs_revision,reject}`. Packet `commands`
entries remain exact CLI compatibility fallbacks and id references.

While working a single packet, call `work.heartbeat` periodically during long
local work such as source reading, edits, tests, or external review. Honor the
packet's `lease.heartbeat_after_seconds`; a lease that stops heartbeating can be
classified as stalled even while you are active locally.

## Front-matter kinds

When publishing Markdown artifacts whose kind has a registered
schema, include the front matter the publisher expects. The
allowed kinds in this runner version are:

- action_item_ledger
- auto_finalize_gate_evidence
- commit_request
- decision
- escalation
- finding
- findings_ledger
- handoff
- harness_improvement_proposal
- marker
- operator_brief
- operator_report
- other
- patch_summary
- pr_request
- progress_note
- prompt
- support_ledger
- synthesis
- test_report
- work_plan

The publisher refuses invalid front matter with exit code 6.

Paste `expected_artifacts[].author_line` exactly when you include `author:`
in front matter. Common schema skeletons:

### `finding`

```yaml
---
schema_version: striatum.finding.v1
artifact_kind: finding
verdict_intent: accept   # one of: accept, accept_with_findings, needs_revision, reject
constraint_discharge: []   # optional; list of objects
severity: info   # optional; one of: info, low, medium, high, critical
tags: []   # optional; list of strings
---
```

### `findings_ledger`

```yaml
---
schema_version: striatum.findings_ledger.v1
artifact_kind: findings_ledger
summary_count: 0   # non-negative integer
constraint_discharge: []   # optional; list of objects
entries_path: "<value>"   # optional
---
```

### `synthesis`

```yaml
---
schema_version: striatum.synthesis.v1
artifact_kind: synthesis
inputs: []   # optional; list of upstream artifact refs
---
```

### `support_ledger`

```yaml
---
schema_version: striatum.support_ledger.v1
artifact_kind: support_ledger
audited_artifact: "<value>"
claim_count: 0   # optional; non-negative integer
---
```

### `action_item_ledger`

```yaml
---
schema_version: striatum.action_item_ledger.v1
artifact_kind: action_item_ledger
revision_round: 0   # non-negative integer
source_review_artifact: "<value>"
total_items: 0   # optional; non-negative integer
---
```

### `collaboration_ledger`

```yaml
---
schema_version: striatum.collaboration_ledger.v1
artifact_kind: collaboration_ledger
entries: []   # non-empty list of objects
participants: "<value>"
rationale: "<value>"
shape: falsification_gate   # one of: falsification_gate, cross_examination, fog_of_war_review, synaptic_prune, adjudicated_constraint_extraction
topic: "<value>"
verdict: accept   # one of: accept, accept_with_findings, needs_revision, reject
adjudication_mode: single   # optional; one of: single, second_on_disagreement
adjudicators: "<value>"   # optional
branches: "<value>"   # optional
constraints: "<value>"   # optional
cycle: "<value>"   # optional
findings: "<value>"   # optional
---
```

### `escalation`

```yaml
---
schema_version: striatum.escalation.v1
artifact_kind: escalation
blocker_kind: ambiguous_goal   # one of: ambiguous_goal, missing_authority, contradicting_decisions, no_available_reviewer_lane, committee_stalemate, override_required
created_at: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"   # RFC3339 timestamp
description: "<value>"
escalation_id: "<value>"
reasoning: "<value>"
requested_action: "<value>"
run_id: "<value>"
severity: info   # one of: info, low, medium, high, critical
job_id: "<value>"   # optional
related_artifacts: "<value>"   # optional
session_id: "<value>"   # optional
---
```

### `harness_improvement_proposal`

```yaml
---
schema_version: striatum.harness_improvement_proposal.v1
artifact_kind: harness_improvement_proposal
expected_benefit: "<value>"
target: prompt   # one of: prompt, workflow, spec, defaults, documentation
risk: "<value>"   # optional
rollback: "<value>"   # optional
---
```

## Long-lived supervised lanes

If the lane's harness profile sets `supervision.compatible: true`, the current
agent-loop path exports MCP endpoint/token context and expects the agent to
call `tools/list` and `work.await_packet`. The older newline-delimited stdin
delivery via `striatum supervise send` remains a CLI compatibility path:

- `striatum supervise start` — Start a long-lived agent CLI for the session.
- `striatum supervise send` — Deliver a packet to a supervisor's stdin pipe.
- `striatum supervise stop` — Stop a supervisor (SIGTERM, SIGKILL after 5s).
- `striatum supervise status` — Probe a supervisor's liveness.
- `striatum supervise list` — List supervisors for a run.

Copy-pasteable supervised claim/send flow:

```bash
SESSION=$(striatum --repo $REPO register-session --run-id $RUN \
    --role $ROLE --lane $LANE --fresh --json | jq -r .data.session_id)
striatum --repo $REPO supervise start --session-id $SESSION --json
CLAIM=$(striatum --repo $REPO claim-next --session-id $SESSION --json)
PACKET_ID=$(printf '%s\n' "$CLAIM" | jq -r .data.packet_id)
striatum --repo $REPO supervise send \
    --session-id $SESSION --packet-id $PACKET_ID --json
```

For MCP, call `work.await_packet` directly instead of routing packets through
stdin. For CLI fallback, use `data.packet_id`, or paste
`data.next_steps.supervise_send`. Do not use `message_id`, `lease_id`,
`job_id`, `session_id`, or `supervisor_id` as `--packet-id`.

## Recovery

When a run looks stuck:

- `striatum status` — Read run/job/blocker state.
- `striatum why` — Explain why a job is in its current state.
- `striatum doctor --verbose` — Surface structured consistency problems.
- `striatum recovery stale-leases` — Lazy-expire and report stale leases.
- `striatum recovery requeue-stale` — Requeue an expired non-repo-write job.
- `striatum recovery process-reconcile` — Reconcile externally-killed processes.
- `striatum recovery resume` — Resolve remediated process-adapter blockers.
- `striatum recovery complete-stalled` — Finalize a dead lane's job from its durable artifacts instead of hand-capturing the worktree (D200).
- `striatum recovery resolve-blocker` — Close a dangling non-escalation, non-checkpoint blocker that no completion path cleared (#304).
- `striatum checkpoint resolve` — Resolve a `human_checkpoint` blocker.
- `striatum dashboard --once` — Render a single dashboard frame for scripts.

Common pattern:

```bash
striatum --repo $REPO status --run-id $RUN --json
striatum --repo $REPO why $JOB_OR_RUN --json
striatum --repo $REPO doctor --run-id $RUN --verbose --json
```

## MCP Mutation Surface

Use this section when an operator gives you a capability token, when you are
driving live workflow control, or when chat workflow generation needs
preview/write tool calls.

Call `tools/list` first. It returns the effective supported production tool
set for the current token after capability, repository-scope, and production
visibility filters. Local workflow-file authoring methods and retired
dogfood composites are hidden from discovery. `tools/call` re-authorizes
every call; mutating calls append metadata-only audit rows, including denials.
Use `daemon.hello` / `daemon.welcome` for version handshake and
`daemon.describe` when the operator needs to inspect the broader method
registry.

Preview generated workflows with `workflow.generate.preview` when it appears
in `tools/list`; it returns the workflow, file list, graph metadata, warnings,
and validation without writing files. Workflow-file authoring writes use the
web-chat workflow-authoring flow or CLI compatibility fallback and may not be
discoverable through production daemon MCP `tools/list`.

Denial recovery:

| Denial | Agent response |
|---|---|
| `capability_missing` | Stop and ask the operator for a short-lived token with the named capability and correct repository scope. |
| `token_revoked` | Stop retrying; treat revocation as an operator decision. |
| `token_expired` | Ask for a fresh token with the same narrow scope. |
| `method_unknown` | Re-read `tools/list`; if absent, ask the operator to inspect `daemon.describe` for version skew. |
| `mutations_disabled` | Do not retry. The operator must restart the service with `--allow-mutations` to permit writes. |

A repo-scoped write token for repo A cannot write repo B. Do not request
wildcard or admin capabilities for ordinary generation, do not bypass
the daemon by opening Postgres directly or treating `.striatum/` scratch files as workflow state, and do not treat audit as malicious-local-root-
resistant proof.

## What not to do

- Do not bypass the daemon (the CLI is the only client; the daemon is the single writer per D094 / RFC 0043); never open Postgres directly, and do not treat `.striatum/` scratch files as workflow state.
- Do not treat marker files, tmux panes, or terminal output as workflow state.
- Do not advance state by printing phrases; advance by calling the CLI verbs in your work packet.
- Do not capture stdout/stderr transcripts; D028 keeps them off by default.
- Do not derive bylines from job titles; use the byline supplied in your work packet.
- Do not parse a supervisor's own output for workflow state; supervisors send DEVNULL.
- Do not paste over a broken runner: never hand-finish stranded or wedged work (manual worktree capture, cherry-pick, or hand-commit) and report it complete, and never proceed while `doctor` is red — recover through the daemon (`recovery requeue-stale`/`resume`/`complete-stalled`, `checkpoint resolve`) or surface the defect (file an issue, record the friction, escalate) instead of masking it as a success.
